## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
# Install the latest version from GitHub if needed
# Uncomment these lines to install the GitHub version:
# if (!require(remotes)) install.packages("remotes")
# remotes::install_github("r-causal/ggdag")

library(ggdag)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

# Create the DAG structure - try without custom labels first
# Treatment -> Censoring <- Measured Confounder -> Outcome
selection_dag_simple <- dagify(
  Censoring ~ Treatment + Age,
  Outcome ~ Age,
  exposure = "Treatment",
  outcome = "Outcome",
  coords = list(
    x = c(Treatment = 1, Age = 3, Censoring = 2, Outcome = 4),
    y = c(Treatment = 2, Age = 2, Censoring = 1, Outcome = 2)
  )
)

cat("Checking simple DAG object class:\n")
cat("Class of selection_dag_simple:", class(selection_dag_simple), "\n")

# Convert to tidy_dagitty explicitly
tidy_selection_dag <- tidy_dagitty(selection_dag_simple)
cat("Class of tidy_selection_dag:", class(tidy_selection_dag), "\n")

# Check the structure of the tidy object
cat("\nStructure of tidy_dagitty object:\n")
str(tidy_selection_dag)

# Check what dagitty sees as exposure and outcome
cat("Exposure variables:", dagitty::exposures(selection_dag_simple), "\n")
cat("Outcome variables:", dagitty::outcomes(selection_dag_simple), "\n")

# Try dag_paths with the simple version
cat("\nTrying dag_paths with simple DAG (no custom labels):\n")
try({
  paths_result <- dag_paths(tidy_selection_dag, from = "Treatment", to = "Outcome")
  print(paths_result)
}, silent = FALSE)

# If that works, add labels as a separate step
if (exists("paths_result")) {
  cat("\nSuccess! Now trying with labels added separately:\n")
  # Add labels to the existing tidy object
  tidy_selection_dag$data$label <- case_when(
    tidy_selection_dag$data$name == "Treatment" ~ "Treatment",
    tidy_selection_dag$data$name == "Age" ~ "Age\n(Measured)",
    tidy_selection_dag$data$name == "Censoring" ~ "Censoring", 
    tidy_selection_dag$data$name == "Outcome" ~ "Outcome",
    TRUE ~ tidy_selection_dag$data$name
  )
}

# Plot the basic DAG using the working version
p1 <- ggdag(tidy_selection_dag, text = FALSE, use_labels = "name") +
  theme_dag_blank() +
  labs(title = "Selection Bias via Collider: Measured Confounder",
       subtitle = "Censoring is a collider of Treatment and Age") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(p1)

# Show what happens when we condition on censoring (selection)
# This opens a backdoor path: Treatment <- Censoring -> Age -> Outcome
p2 <- selection_dag %>%
  control_for("Censoring") %>%
  ggdag_adjust(text = FALSE, use_labels = "label") +
  theme_dag_blank() +
  labs(title = "Conditioning on Censoring (Analyzing Only Completers)",
       subtitle = "Opens backdoor path: Treatment ← Censoring → Age → Outcome",
       caption = "Red = Conditioned variable, Blue = Adjusted paths") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(p2)

# Show the paths - ensuring proper object class
cat("Checking DAG object class:\n")
cat("Class of selection_dag:", class(selection_dag), "\n")

# Convert to tidy_dagitty explicitly
tidy_selection_dag <- tidy_dagitty(selection_dag)
cat("Class of tidy_selection_dag:", class(tidy_selection_dag), "\n")

# Check what dagitty sees as exposure and outcome
cat("Exposure variables:", dagitty::exposures(selection_dag), "\n")
cat("Outcome variables:", dagitty::outcomes(selection_dag), "\n")

# Try dag_paths with the tidy version
cat("\nTrying dag_paths with tidy_dagitty object:\n")
paths_result <- dag_paths(tidy_selection_dag, from = "Treatment", to = "Outcome")
print(paths_result)

# Visualize the paths using the tidy version
p_paths <- ggdag_paths(tidy_selection_dag, from = "Treatment", to = "Outcome",
                       text = FALSE, use_labels = "label") +
  theme_dag_blank() +
  labs(title = "All Paths from Treatment to Outcome",
       subtitle = "Note: No open paths in original DAG (blocked by collider)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(p_paths)

# Show what adjustment for Age does (it doesn't help!)
p3 <- selection_dag %>%
  control_for(c("Censoring", "Age")) %>%
  ggdag_adjust(text = FALSE, use_labels = "label") +
  theme_dag_blank() +
  labs(title = "Adjusting for Age After Conditioning on Censoring",
       subtitle = "Bias remains because we're adjusting post-selection",
       caption = "Adjustment cannot fix the collider bias created by selection") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(p3)

# Alternative view showing the problem more clearly
# Let's add a selection indicator
selection_dag_explicit <- dagify(
  Censoring ~ Treatment + Age,
  Outcome ~ Age,
  Observed ~ Censoring,  # We only observe when not censored
  coords = list(
    x = c(Treatment = 1, Age = 3, Censoring = 2, Outcome = 4, Observed = 2),
    y = c(Treatment = 2, Age = 2, Censoring = 1.5, Outcome = 2, Observed = 0.5)
  ),
  labels = c(
    Treatment = "Treatment",
    Age = "Age\n(Measured)",
    Censoring = "Censoring",
    Outcome = "Outcome",
    Observed = "Observed\n(Selection)"
  )
)

p4 <- ggdag(selection_dag_explicit, text = FALSE, use_labels = "label") +
  theme_dag_blank() +
  labs(title = "Explicit Selection Process",
       subtitle = "We can only analyze cases where Observed = 1 (not censored)") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5))

print(p4)
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).
